q: Why Self-Employed Income Can Look Complicated to a Bank
text: Most banks assess self-employed income using rigid, PAYG-shaped rules, two years of tax returns, no addbacks considered properly, and no understanding of how trust distributions, company structures, or fluctuating year-on-year revenue actually work. So a business owner earning genuinely more than the number on their tax return gets assessed as if they earn less, or gets declined outright because their income “looks inconsistent.” It isn’t inconsistent. It’s just not being read correctly. Our expert home loan brokers specialise in navigating complex income structures and finding a strategic way forward, helping you understand your options and identify finance that fits your circumstances. We know which lenders use low-doc and alt-doc policies properly, which will add back depreciation and one-off business costs, which understand trust and company structures without treating them as a red flag, and which will look at a single strong year rather than penalising you for an average across two.

A business loan gives your company capital to grow, cover a shortfall, or move on an opportunity. Businesses use this funding to expand, buy stock, hire staff, or manage cash flow through a slow patch. Not all business loans work the same way. Lenders price and structure them differently depending on your revenue, trading history, and what you can offer as security. Some business owners put up assets, such as property, inventory, or invoices, as collateral. Others choose an unsecured loan to move faster, without pledging anything at all. Getting this choice right is a strategy decision, not a paperwork exercise. It shapes your rate, your repayment terms, and how much flexibility you keep for what comes next.

The difference comes down to one question: does the lender need collateral? A secured loan is backed by an asset you own, such as property, equipment, or inventory. An unsecured loan isn’t backed by anything beyond your business’s ability to repay it.

Secured loans typically come with lower interest rates and more flexible terms because the lender carries less risk. In exchange, you’ll provide an asset as security and generally need to provide more documentation along the way.

Unsecured loans don’t require collateral. Instead, lenders assess your cash flow, trading history, and sometimes a director’s validation, to decide what you qualify for. Because there’s no asset backing the loan, lenders treat it as higher risk and price it with a higher interest rate to match. Even so, many small business owners choose unsecured finance. When you need funds fast and don’t want to tie up property or equipment, the speed can be worth the trade-off. The right call depends on your business, your timeline, and what you’re trying to achieve, which is exactly what we work through with you before recommending anything.

q: What Is Asset and Equipment Finance?
text: Asset finance lets you put equipment, vehicles, or technology to work in your business now, and pay for it over time, instead of finding a large amount upfront. It’s built to protect your cash flow while your business gets the productivity boost that new equipment brings. “Asset finance” and “equipment finance” often get used as if they’re the same thing, but there’s a difference. Asset finance is the broader term. It covers vehicles, technology, and other equipment a growing business needs. Equipment finance sits inside that, covering the machinery your industry runs on, from heavy plants for mining to commercial kitchen gear for hospitality.

q: What Can You Use Asset Finance For?
text: Use asset finance to acquire equipment, vehicles or technology, and spread the cost over manageable monthly repayments instead of one upfront hit. Structured well, asset financing keeps cash in the business for necessary expenses: wages, stock, marketing, or the next opportunity. Small and medium Australian businesses use asset finance across almost every sector for exactly this reason. It lets growth happen without draining the account first. Depending on your situation, an asset loan can be secured against the item you’re buying or against another asset you already own. We work out which structure suits your business before recommending anything.

Whether you’re buying your first home, self-employed with a salary that doesn’t fit the standard template, or a business owner navigating a more complex lending situation, we look beyond the obvious to find a strategy that fits your situation. Complex lending isn’t about forcing your circumstances into a lender’s formula. It’s about understanding how your income, goals, and financial position work together, then finding a lending pathway that makes sense. And sometimes, the right advice isn’t to refinance or take on a new loan. Sometimes, it’s knowing that the loan you already have is the right one to keep. For home loans and other consumer credit, the law requires us to act in your benefit. We believe that’s not just a requirement. It’s the standard good advice should meet!

We aim to be more than the broker you call when you need a loan. We aim to be the partner you call before the next big financial decision, whether you’re buying your first home, building a business, navigating complex lending, or planning your next investment. Our vision is to build relationships that last beyond a single transaction, with advice that evolves as your circumstances, goals, and opportunities change. Because your finance strategy shouldn’t just work for where you are today. It should keep working for where you’re going next.

I’m Priya Dey, Founder and Director of Finance Square Group, a finance professional, business owner, property enthusiast and mum of two. I started Finance Square because I wanted to build the kind of finance business I would want to deal with myself: knowledgeable and strategic, but also personal, approachable and genuinely interested in what you’re trying to achieve. I hold a Diploma in Finance and Mortgage Broking and have extensive experience across residential, investment, commercial and business finance. Over the years, I’ve worked with people at very different stages of life: first home buyers, homeowners, property investors, self-employed borrowers and business owners. Some situations are simple. Others involve businesses, multiple income streams, investments or circumstances that banks struggle to categorise. That experience has reinforced something I strongly believe: finance is personal. My approach is simple: understand the person first, then the numbers. And I’ll probably challenge you to think beyond “How much can I borrow?” and instead ask: “What actually makes sense for the life I’m trying to build?” Home | Business | Investment | Asset Refinance Australia-based mort

q: What Your First 3 Steps Would Look Like
text: Wherever you’re starting from, the process begins with understanding your situation, not pushing you towards a particular lender.

We begin with a focused 15-minute conversation about your goals, timeline, income, and financial position. Whether you’re buying your first home, self-employed with income that doesn’t fit the standard template, or running a business with more complex lending needs, we start with the full picture.

We assess your circumstances and compare suitable options across our panel of Australian lenders. We explain the trade-offs in plain language, including when the smartest strategy may be to keep your existing loan rather than refinance.

text: Once you decide to proceed, we prepare and manage your application, liaise with the lender and keep everything moving through to settlement. You have one broker who knows your situation and stays with you throughout the journey.

q: 6. Consumer and Business Lending Are Treated Differently
text: Some of our services, particularly through FNSQ Business and FNSQ Asset, relate to credit provided wholly or predominantly for business purposes. Business-purpose credit is generally not regulated under the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (Cth) in the same way as consumer credit, such as most home loans arranged through FNSQ Home. This means some consumer protections referenced on this Website, including responsible lending obligations, may not apply in the same way to a business loan or an equipment finance facility. We’ll always tell you clearly which rules apply to your specific application.

We want to know if something’s gone wrong. Every complaint gets looked at properly, and we use what we learn to do better. This policy explains how to make a complaint, what happens after you do, and what to do if you’re not satisfied with our response.

A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction about our services, our staff, or a decision we’ve made, where you’d like us to look into it or do something about it. This can relate to a loan application, advice you’ve received, how we’ve communicated with you, or anything else connected to your dealings with Finance Square Group.

We hope you’re delighted with our services. If you’re not, please notify your credit assistance provider first, so we get the chance to put it right directly: Explain the details of your complaint as clearly as you can. You can do this verbally or in writing, and you don’t need to use the word “complaint” for us to treat it as one.
When we receive a complaint, we’ll attempt to resolve it promptly. If your complaint is going to take longer than 30 days to resolve, we’ll notify you in writing to let you know.

If your complaint can’t be resolved directly with your credit assistance provider, please contact our Internal Complaints Officer: Priya Dey, Internal Complaints Officer 0450 355 604 | info@fnsq.com.au

If we don’t reach an agreement on your complaint through our internal process, you can refer it to our External Dispute Resolution (EDR) provider, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). AFCA is the single ASIC-approved external dispute resolution scheme for the Australian credit industry. AFCA provides fair and independent financial services complaint resolution that is free to consumers.

Phone: 1800 931 678 (call, 9am–5pm AEST/AEDT weekdays) Mail: GPO Box 3, Melbourne VIC 3001 There’s no cost to you to lodge a complaint with AFCA. You can also request further details about our dispute resolution procedures, and about our Privacy Policy, at any time.
